ios.desc:
Tired of infinite feeds that leave you feeling drained? Reelly is short-form content—but for your brain. Think of it as the anti-TikTok: bite-sized knowledge drops designed to feed your curiosity, not fry your attention span.

Scroll through captivating micro-articles that combine stunning visuals with surprising insights, curated just for you. No viral fluff. No dance trends. Just pure, brain-tingling learning you can enjoy in under a minute.

Whether you’re sipping your morning coffee or dodging an afternoon slump, Reelly turns idle swiping into something that actually sticks.

Features:
■ AI-Generated Summaries: Enhanced by AI, with each article linked back to its foundational Wikipedia page, YouTube video or Podcast
■ Right swipe to drill further: Each Article is a carousel with multiple right-swipable cards
■ Deep Dive into Topics: Scroll within Topics to learn more. Get lost in a rabbit hole of learning
■ Personalized Content Feed: Enjoy endless articles customized to your preferences, interactions, and shares, thanks to our AI-driven platform vetted

Explore, learn, and grow with Reelly—the smarter way to satisfy your curiosity and embrace the joy of learning.

Download Reelly today and start your journey of discovery!

show_hn.title: Show HN: I made a Wikipedia mobile app, but scrollable and AI summarized

quotes.text:
This has been a side project for about a year, have thought about it ever since ChatGPT came out :)

Mark your interests --> get a feed of short articles tailored for that

Free text search: Search on e.g. "Explorers" --> The app crawls Wikipedia and pulls together a short feed (e.g. Columbus, Vasco da Gama etc.,)

I rewrite the Wikipedia articles with GPT-4o, and store them in a database. When a user searches for something not in the database, I use various models to classify what the user is after (how wide the topic is) and pull together a nice selection of articles and images based on the user input. Hitting the right balance of generation speed with article quality was the most challenging part.

Would really appreciate some feedback, especially if you tend to browse Wikipedia a lot, plus if Simo Häyhä rings any bells (a lot of WW1 + 2 articles at the moment)
